newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products-Refiners drive Gulf gasoline up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products-Refiners drive Gulf gasoline up.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials jumped higher by late Thursday, as players sought to cover short positions ahead of a scheduling deadline on Friday.

Gasoline prices in New York Harbor remained nearly flat Thursday, though some traders pointed to expectations for fewer European cargos destined for the East Coast as foreshadowing a possible rally in the coming days.
On the NYMEX, June heating oil gained 0.25 cent to settle at 57.0 cents, while June gasoline finished up 0.40 cent at 66.93 cents.
- U.S. GULF COAST

Prompt conventional M1 gasoline was talked between about 1.60 and 1.80 cents under the June NYMEX, up more than 1.00 cent from late Wednesday levels, with parcels changing hands at 1.80 cents under the June.
Heavy refiner buying ahead of a scheduling deadline earlier this week drove conventional M1 gasoline differentials sharply higher, though some of that strength dissipated by late Wednesday.

Traders said much of that early-week buying in the M1 grade was short coverng done on a spread basis, with some refiners simply rolling shorts ahead to the Friday scheduling deadline. That could drive the volatile M1 gasoline sharply up on Friday, players said.
- CARGOES

Gasoline cargoes to the U.S. Atlantic Coast will be fairly modest for the next two weeks, players said, with European refiners cutting output and U.K refiners reluctant to sell barrels ahead of possible tax code changes there.
"They'll get a bit of a windfall for barrels in tank over there," one trader said. "And Europe has really dried up recently," the trader added.
"That's one of the reasons the gasoline is starting to move up. People realize we're not seeing the typical flows we normally see," another trader said.

European sources put shipments to the U.S. from Europe between 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes from mid-May through June 5, or an average of as much as 85,000 barrels per day, though some U.S. sources said that figure was slightly too low.
- MIDCONTINENT

Differentials headed lower, paring gains made on buying by Marathon to cover supply obligations since taking ts 166,000 barrel per day Robinson, Ill. refinery into maintenance. Delivery deferral due to operational snags on the Explorer pipeline also boosted product values in recent days.
Group three low sulphur was 5.25 to 5.50 over the June NYMEX, falling from 5.75 to 6.00 cents though still above the 5.00 to 5.25 values Wednesday.
Group three premium retained its firmer level of 3.25 over June futures versus Wednesday's level at 2.75 to 3.00 cents over.
In the Chicago markets, premium gasoline eased further, falling to 4.25 cents over June NYMEX compared with 5.00 cents earlier in the day and 5.25 cents Wednesday.
- NEW YORK HARBOR
Activity remained thin, traders said, with little price movement during the day.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline differentials remained steady, with barrels talked between about 2.00 and 2.25 cents under the June NYMEX.
However, many Harbor players were expecting gasoline prices there to firm because of relatively modest amount of gasoline coming in from Europe.
